Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: Tax schedules are local: whether a specific poultry parcel follows a municipal schedule or the provincial rural regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11: due July 2, 5% on amounts unpaid July 2, further 5% on amounts unpaid October 31; Surveyor of Taxes) depends on where the parcel sits — a per-parcel check, not a province-wide statement. Parcel-level ALR status, zoning, servicing, floodplain position and tax schedule for any specific property: Not verified at parcel level.

faq.a: HPAI is reportable to the CFIA; in a primary control zone, permits are required to move birds, eggs and by-products, and on a quarantined farm nothing bird-related moves without CFIA permission — placements, showings and completion dates can all be delayed. Confirm the property's control-zone status before fixing a completion date.
faq.q: What happens during an avian influenza outbreak?

faq.a: Check the ALR status, water source and licences, drainage and flood history, the buildings and any quota or production licences that do or do not transfer with the land. Poultry and egg production in BC are supply-managed, so a sale of the farm does not automatically include quota.
faq.q: What should I check before buying a farm in BC?

faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is farmland protected by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission. Farm use is generally allowed on ALR land, but subdividing, adding homes or using the land for non-farm purposes usually needs approval, so check a property's ALR status before you offer.
